clue.text: Muse in sloop on Derwent

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, spanning their word breaks

parts.note: the letters run across the end of sloop, all of on, and the start of Derwent

explanation.surface: A poet finds inspiration while sailing a small boat on the River Derwent in the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muse' looks like a noun, the poet's inspiration, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to think something over quietly, a close synonym of the verb in the grid.

clue.text: Assassin's proposal?

definitions.note: the clue's possessive is just surface; the definition is the noun
definitions.meaning: first meaning, playful: one who 'offs' people, slang for kills
second meaning: something put forward for acceptance

explanation.walkthrough: To 'off' someone is slang for killing them, so the question mark allows a jokey coinage for an assassin.
explanation.definitionFit: Read one way it is a noun for a killer; normally it is a bid or proposition put to someone.

clue.text: Difficult to follow the German action film?

indicators.note: to follow means to come after, so the first word goes behind the second

parts.note: die is a German word for the
hard means difficult

explanation.surface: A German film is hard to keep up with.
explanation.definitionFit: Die Hard is the 1988 Bruce Willis film, a classic of the action genre.

clue.text: Rocky outcrop to climb — and perish!

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means going upwards, so the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hilltop, common on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A climber scales a crag and comes to grief.
explanation.definitionFit: To rot is to decay and so perish, as organic matter does.

clue.text: Fill drinking vessel coy drunk holds

indicators.note: the jumbled word holds the vessel, keeping it inside itself
someone drunk is all over the place, so the letters of coy stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a cup is a vessel you drink from

explanation.surface: Someone shy is getting drunk while filling up a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: To occupy a space or a role is to fill it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Officers at first lie badly, bent in court

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter only

parts.note: the first letter of Officers

indicators.note: something bent is twisted out of shape, so those letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as the fodder

explanation.surface: Corrupt police officers give poor false testimony in a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' is British slang for corrupt, which makes it look like a description of the officers. The Old Bailey is London's Central Criminal Court.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Bailey is the familiar name of England's best-known criminal court building.

clue.text: Agree that man should come into church

indicators.note: coming into something means entering it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
him refers to that man

explanation.surface: A congregation agrees a certain man should join their church.
explanation.definitionFit: To chime with something is to be in harmony with it, idiomatically to agree.

clue.text: Spotted baked dish — no cover on top?

parts.note: a pie is a baked dish
having no hair on your head means being bald

explanation.surface: A cook notices an open pie with no pastry lid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' looks like 'noticed', but it is the adjective for patchy colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: A piebald horse has irregular black and white patches, so it is spotted or blotched.

clue.text: Feigned and fanciful fact-feed

indicators.note: fanciful means imaginative or invented, so the letters are rearranged freely

parts.note: all eight letters of the hyphenated word are the fodder

explanation.surface: A news feed full of pretend facts is fake and fanciful.
explanation.definitionFit: An affected manner or emotion is put on for show, just as a feigned one is pretended.

clue.text: Individual article or a couple?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a single thing on a list
second meaning: two people romantically linked

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the informal second sense: a pair who are seeing each other are called an item.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means one separate thing in a set, and colloquially a pair in a relationship.

clue.text: Any number leaving stadium locality

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter is dropped from the word for stadium

parts.note: an arena is a sports stadium
N stands for an unspecified number in algebra

explanation.surface: A crowd of any size is filing out of the stadium into the surrounding district.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a district or neighbourhood, which is what a locality means.

clue.text: Small step taken by male astronaut

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a pace is a single step
a man is a male person

explanation.surface: Echoes Neil Armstrong's 'one small step for man' on the Moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaceman is an informal word for someone who travels into space, an astronaut.

clue.text: Firm dates fixed without delay

indicators.note: something fixed has been repaired or altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
fast means quickly, with no delay

explanation.surface: Appointments have been settled promptly and definitely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixed' reads like 'arranged', which suits dates, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadfast means resolute and unwavering, which is firm in the sense of loyal.

clue.text: This helps when changing banks

parts.note: surface reading: something useful when moving your account from one bank to another
setter's reading: crossing from one river bank to the other

explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' makes you think of money; here they are the sides of a river, and the structure helps you cross over.
explanation.definitionFit: The thing spans a river so people can get from one side to the opposite one.

clue.text: Roll about one and make merry

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the list wraps around the numeral

parts.note: a roll is a list of names, a roster
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A reveller tumbles around and has fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll about' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'Roll' is a noun meaning a list.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to celebrate noisily, an old-fashioned word for making merry.

clue.text: Urge one to join Liberal Party

parts.note: LIB is the usual abbreviation for Liberal
I is the Roman numeral for one
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Political canvassing: a plea for someone to sign up with the Liberal Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is sexual desire, a strong drive or urge.

clue.text: Dress circle next to stage — no way!

parts.note: a band is a ring or circle

indicators.note: no way says a road abbreviation is removed from the word before it

parts.note: taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A theatregoer refuses a seat in the dress circle beside the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress circle' reads as the theatre balcony; split it, and dress is the verb, as in dressing a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: To bandage a wound is to dress it, wrapping it in a protective strip.

clue.text: Celebration third at sea, within cove

indicators.note: the mixed letters sit inside the word for cove

parts.note: a cove is a small bay

indicators.note: being at sea means being confused, so those letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A party held on the third day of a voyage, in a sheltered cove.
explanation.definitionFit: A birthday is the anniversary of someone's birth, usually marked with a party.

clue.text: Story involving British data chart

indicators.note: involving means including, so the story takes the letter inside it

parts.note: a tale is a story
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A report about Britain with statistics laid out in a chart.
explanation.definitionFit: A table sets out information in rows and columns, a kind of chart for data.

clue.text: Name is French for snug retreat

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A language lesson: the word for a cosy hideaway is given in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest is a cosy, sheltered place to retreat to, figuratively from a bird's home.

clue.text: South African money gets material

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa or South African
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone from South Africa spends cash on cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a glossy woven fabric, a type of cloth or material.

clue.text: Hurt toe — slippery start with bath?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of slippery
a tub is a bath

explanation.surface: Someone slips getting into the bath and knocks their toe.
explanation.definitionFit: To stub is to bump your toe painfully against something, so it means hurting the toe.

clue.text: Ordering option: porter brought round a trolley

indicators.note: the drink is brought round the others, wrapping around them on both sides

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale
taken as written
a cart is a trolley

explanation.surface: A hotel porter wheels a trolley round for someone ordering room service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a hotel worker but is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: In a restaurant, ordering a la carte means choosing individually priced dishes rather than a set menu.

clue.text: Fool in Tarsus regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of Tarsus

explanation.surface: An idiot regularly turns up in Tarsus, the Turkish city where St Paul was born.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a foolish person, from the donkey's reputation for stupidity.

clue.text: Old City man politely pressing

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
gent is short for gentleman, the polite word for a man

explanation.surface: An elderly City of London banker is courteously insistent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' suggests London's financial district; here it is Ur, the ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pressing demands immediate attention, which is what urgent means.

clue.text: Stuart queen is turning brown

indicators.note: turning round makes the words face the other way, so they are read backwards

parts.note: Queen Anne was the last Stuart monarch
taken as written

explanation.surface: A royal Stuart is changing colour, perhaps from a tan.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earth pigment giving a yellowish or reddish brown, so it names a brown shade.
